advisories.title: Chrome before 156.0.8078.73: four critical bugs reachable from a web page; agent browsers without the sandbox are most exposed
advisories.summary: Google's Chrome stable update of 2026-10-27 fixed four bugs that Chromium rates Critical: memory corruption in FileSystem that can run code outside the sandbox (CVE-2026-118306), and three that can run code inside the renderer sandbox (FileAPI, Skia and Layout). All are triggered by a crafted HTML page and affect Google Chrome before 156.0.8078.73. Browsers launched by automation without the Chromium sandbox, which is the Playwright library and test-runner default, lose the containment that normally stops the three renderer bugs at the sandbox. No stable Playwright release pins a fixed Chrome for Testing build yet.

severity.rationale: A web page alone can trigger all four bugs, and CVE-2026-118306 can run code outside the sandbox. Agents open pages unattended, so the user-interaction precondition is met without a person, and automation browsers often run without the sandbox, which removes containment for the other three. No exploitation is known.

exploitation.note: Not in CISA KEV catalog version 2026.10.30; CISA SSVC on the NVD records marks exploitation as none; the Chrome release notes do not report exploitation.

affected.note: Same browser builds as Chrome; check the executable's --version.
Playwright 1.64.0 and 1.64.1 pin Chrome for Testing 156.0.8078.4 (revision 1248); 1.63.0 pins 153.0.8010.12 (revision 1243). No stable release pins a fixed build as of 2026-11-03.

advisories.exposure: Most exposed: browsers driven by agents, scrapers or scripts that visit pages you do not control, especially when launched without the Chromium sandbox (Playwright's chromium.launch() and launchPersistentContext() add --no-sandbox unless chromiumSandbox is true; channel 'chrome' alone does not change that). Exposed: any Google Chrome or Chrome for Testing before 156.0.8078.73 used to browse. Lower exposure: Playwright's pinned test builds used only against your own trusted application. Playwright MCP and the Playwright CLI default to the installed Chrome with the sandbox on, so in that default configuration they are covered once Chrome is updated; on Linux, Playwright MCP disables the sandbox by default for downloaded Chromium channels, and both accept sandbox overrides, so check the actual executable, version and flags of any non-default setup.

detectors.note: Classify a browser as test-only only when it is confirmed to process solely the owner's trusted application; otherwise treat it as browsing. A cache path such as ms-playwright does not establish context.
A running unsandboxed browser below the fixed version is the most severe finding.

remediation.details: Update Google Chrome, Chromium or Edge to a build that includes the 2026-10-27 fixes (Chrome 156.0.8078.73 or later) and restart every running instance; a running process keeps the old code until it restarts.
remediation.risk: Low. Restarting closes open tabs and may interrupt automation sessions that are running.

remediation.action: Agent and scraper browsers launched with the Playwright library
remediation.details: Launch the patched installed Chrome with the sandbox on: chromium.launch({ channel: 'chrome', chromiumSandbox: true }). Do not point Playwright's downloaded builds or Chrome for Testing at untrusted pages: Google states Chrome for Testing should only be used to consume trustworthy content. Branded Chrome removed the command-line flags for side-loading unpacked extensions, so automation that needs an unpacked extension cannot use this path and should not browse untrusted pages with an unsandboxed or test build instead. On Linux distributions that restrict unprivileged user namespaces with AppArmor, a downloaded Chromium build refuses to start with the sandbox on unless a root-owned setuid sandbox helper (CHROME_DEVEL_SANDBOX) or an AppArmor profile is installed, which is safer than falling back to --no-sandbox.
remediation.risk: Medium. Switching browser build can change behavior of existing profiles and extensions; test the automation flows after the change.

remediation.details: Keep pinned test browsers for your own trusted application only, and upgrade Playwright when a release pins a Chrome for Testing build at or above 156.0.8078.73. Do not point them at third-party sites.
remediation.risk: Low.

verification: Run each Google Chrome and Chrome for Testing executable used to browse with --version and confirm 156.0.8078.73 or later. Edge, Brave and other Chromium derivatives use their own version numbers: confirm the fix in that vendor's security release notes.
Open chrome://sandbox in the automation browser and confirm it reports that you are adequately sandboxed.
List running processes and confirm no Chromium-family browser used for browsing runs with --no-sandbox.
Re-run the automation flows that depend on the browser (sign-in profiles, extensions) and confirm they still work.

sources.quote: The Stable channel has been updated to 156.0.8078.73/.74 for Windows and Mac and 156.0.8078.73 to Linux
It should only be used to consume trustworthy content.

discovery.note: Alert post; directionally right for library and test-runner use, overstated for Playwright MCP and CLI.
Playwright's official account; scope clarification consistent with the tier 1 sources.

review.notes: Re-read the cited primary sources. All prior findings are resolved: MCP/CLI defaults and Linux exceptions, detector context, vendor-specific version checks, trusted-content guidance, extension flags, exact quote and release evidence. No unsupported or misleading claim requiring changes remains. Validation reports only the eight expected review-placeholder problems.

advisories.title: praktor Telegram uploads can overwrite persistent agent instructions
advisories.summary: A Telegram document filename can escape the uploads directory and overwrite files in the persistent agent workspace. This can plant instructions or execution configuration consumed by later agent runs.

severity.rationale: Remote file writes reach persistent agent instructions. Messaging the bot is sufficient with the default unrestricted sender policy, making unattended agents especially exposed.

advisories.exposure: Exposed when untrusted Telegram users can send documents to the bot; an empty sender allowlist permits everyone.

remediation.details: Upgrade to 0.9.1. Until then, restrict telegram.allow_from to trusted sender IDs.
remediation.risk: Low. Test dependent workflows after updating.

advisories.summary: Elo has three independent injection flaws: JavaScript constructor access can execute host code, Ruby interpolation can execute commands, and unchecked AST fields can inject generated JavaScript, Ruby, Python or SQL.

severity.rationale: Attacker-supplied Elo source can execute code through documented CLI and library paths. CI and agent pipelines that evaluate untrusted expressions expose the host runtime.

affected.note: All three advisories list versions through 1.0.0.

advisories.exposure: Requires processing attacker-controlled Elo source or programmatic ASTs. Ruby injection requires executing the Ruby output; AST injection requires attacker-influenced node fields.

remediation.details: Upgrade to 1.0.1 before evaluating untrusted Elo input.
remediation.risk: Low. Test dependent workflows after updating.

advisories.title: Stanza 1.14.0 can execute code while loading an untrusted lemmatizer checkpoint
advisories.summary: The lemmatizer decompresses and unpickles an inner checkpoint field without restrictions. PyTorch weights_only=True does not protect that inner stream.

severity.rationale: Code execution requires an attacker-controlled custom lemma checkpoint. This is a narrower model-loading configuration, rather than ordinary text inference.

affected.note: The advisory lists exactly 1.14.0 as affected.

advisories.exposure: Pipelines loading caller-supplied or shared untrusted lemma checkpoints are exposed. Ordinary inference text alone is not this attack surface.

params.instructions: Check whether stanza is exactly 1.14.0 and whether custom or shared lemma checkpoints can be untrusted.

remediation.details: Upgrade to 1.15.0, which fixes the unrestricted inner deserialization.
remediation.risk: Low. Test dependent workflows after updating.

verification: Confirm the installed version or revision and exercise the affected workflow with trusted inputs.

advisories.title: Langflow OSS through 1.12.8 has authentication bypass and unauthenticated code execution
advisories.summary: IBM reports authentication bypass and unauthenticated code execution, including an MCP tool-enumeration path. The same upgrade also addresses authenticated agentic command execution and credential disclosure. All four Langflow flaws are addressed by Langflow OSS 1.13.0.

severity.rationale: Unauthenticated remote code execution reaches the agent workflow server. No account or further user interaction is required in the published CVSS vector.

advisories.exposure: Exposed deployments allow attacker access to Langflow, including its MCP surface. Do not assume the authentication control prevents access.

remediation.details: Back up the database, secret key and uploaded files. Prepare automatic-login accounts for password sign-in, then upgrade the package or Docker deployment to 1.13.0.
remediation.risk: Medium. Authentication changes and persistent deployment data require upgrade preparation.

verification: Confirm the installed version or revision and exercise the affected workflow with trusted inputs.

advisories.title: Strands Agents Tools environment tool lets prompt injection disable secret masking
advisories.summary: The model-controlled masked parameter can expose environment secrets through the environment tool. Injected instructions can cause unmasked values to be returned and passed through other tools.

severity.rationale: Untrusted content can cause credential disclosure without operator consent for reads. Credential exposure warrants a 72-hour response in agent environments.

advisories.exposure: Requires an agent loading the environment tool and processing attacker-influenced content. The attack exposes secrets present in the agent process environment.

remediation.details: Upgrade to 0.8.6 or later, or remove the environment tool pending upgrade. Rotate credentials present in environments whose agents loaded this tool.
remediation.risk: Medium. Tool removal and credential rotation can disrupt agents.

verification: Confirm version 0.8.6 or later and that the model cannot control masking; verify credential rotation.

advisories.title: Linux IPv4 TCP use-after-free can permit remote code execution
advisories.summary: The IPv4 TCP connection setup flaw can lead to remote code execution. Ubuntu describes an unreleased exploit using MPTCP and warns that the underlying flaw is not specific to MPTCP.

severity.rationale: Remote kernel code execution threatens developer and agent hosts accepting network connections. No public or in-the-wild exploit claim is established here.

affected.note: Affected branches require vendor-specific backports. Ubuntu blog lists proposed fixes, while the current CVE tracker marks packages as work in progress; confirm the exact release and flavor.

advisories.exposure: Relevant to exposed IPv4 TCP handling. Disabling MPTCP alone is not a complete fix for the underlying vulnerability.

params.instructions: Identify the running kernel, distribution release and kernel flavor; compare the exact package with the vendor CVE tracker and update channel.

remediation.details: Apply the distribution fix and reboot. Ubuntu offers testing fixes through proposed for 22.04 and newer; use acceptance testing and confirm current package status before installation.
remediation.risk: Medium. Kernel replacement requires a reboot; proposed packages need local acceptance testing.

verification: Confirm the running kernel after reboot matches a vendor-confirmed fixed package for the exact kernel flavor.

advisories.title: MoLing SSE mode exposes local MCP tools to malicious web pages
advisories.summary: Unauthenticated SSE endpoints with wildcard CORS let a malicious web page obtain a session identifier and invoke MCP tools. Resulting file access or command execution depends on the configured tools.

severity.rationale: A page can steal the tool session credential and invoke local capabilities. SSE mode and powerful tools are required, so the impact is conditional rather than universal code execution.

advisories.exposure: Requires MoLing running in SSE mode and a browser visiting untrusted content.

params.instructions: Check whether MoLing is version 0.4.0 or earlier and runs in SSE mode with the -l flag.

remediation.details: Upgrade to 0.5.0, which adds token authentication and removes wildcard CORS. Until then avoid SSE mode while exposed to untrusted web content.
remediation.risk: Low. Test dependent workflows after updating.

verification: Confirm version 0.5.0 or later and verify the SSE endpoint requires authentication and refuses cross-origin access.

advisories.title: simple-git argument parser misses the VISUAL editor execution path
advisories.summary: The parser omits VISUAL from unsafe-editor detection. A consumer forwarding attacker-controlled environment values can execute an attacker-selected editor during interactive Git operations.

severity.rationale: Code execution requires a Git operation opening an editor and control over its environment. Such job and agent input flows can defeat the default unsafe-operation guard.

advisories.exposure: Requires an executable attacker-selected editor, suitable TERM and no higher-priority editor override. Consumers without untrusted environment forwarding are not exposed through this path.

remediation.details: Upgrade the parser to 2.0.1. Verify the resolved dependency in applications using simple-git.
remediation.risk: Low. Test dependent workflows after updating.

verification: Confirm the installed version or revision and exercise the affected workflow with trusted inputs.

advisories.summary: The fetch guard resolves an internationalized hostname differently from the HTTP connection. An attacker-controlled URL can reach internal services or cloud metadata and return responses to the agent.

severity.rationale: Fetching attacker URLs is normal for browsing agents. Bypassing the private-address guard can expose sensitive internal responses, including cloud metadata.

remediation.details: Upgrade mcp-server-fetch to 2026.10.24, which aligns the hostname used for checking and connecting.
remediation.risk: Low. Test dependent workflows after updating.

severity.rationale: Code execution requires PandasTools and attacker influence over agent tool calls. Untrusted content influencing a tool-using agent is a common exposure.

affected.note: CVE record lists affected versions through 3.1.11; it specifies no fixed release.

advisories.exposure: Exposed agents load PandasTools and allow model-selected pandas functions to process attacker-controlled paths.

params.instructions: Check whether agno is 3.1.11 or earlier and whether PandasTools exposes model-selected pandas functions.

remediation.details: As a containment recommendation, disconnect PandasTools from untrusted workflows until a vendor-verified fix is deployed. Do not infer that the next numbered version fixes it.
